title: Exterior House Painting: Cost, Prep and Timing
alt: Company painting photo collection: Exterior Painting
excerpt: Plan an exterior house repaint with clear surfaces, preparation, cost factors and suitable painting conditions.

sections.title: Define the exterior painting scope
paragraphs: Walk around the house and list the siding, doors, trim and roofline details you want refreshed. Photograph the whole exterior and close-ups of worn areas. Decide whether the goal is maintenance, a colour change or a smaller update before comparing painting proposals.
Identify the material on each surface if you can. Aluminum, vinyl, wood and masonry have different preparation and coating needs. A shared colour still needs material-specific products.

sections.title: Review preparation before choosing colour
paragraphs: Peeling paint, chalking, damp areas and damaged components need assessment before a repaint. Ask which cleaning, coating removal, repairs and priming are included, and which issues must be resolved separately. New paint cannot repair rotten wood or a failing panel.

Compare suitable colour samples beside roofing, brick and windows that will remain. Check any material-specific restrictions, especially for vinyl, before approving a shade. Keep colour and product details in your notes.

sections.title: Compare exterior painting cost by scope
paragraphs: Exterior house painting cost depends on surface area, material, height, preparation, repairs and access. Extensive peeling changes the preparation needed. Ask for the included surfaces and proposed coating system in writing rather than relying on a generic house-size price.

Confirm whether fascia, soffits, doors and trim are covered. Ask how extra repairs or changes are handled. Compare proposals on the actual work offered, not only the total, and keep any project-specific terms with the agreed scope.

sections.title: Plan suitable weather and access
paragraphs: Late spring through early fall is a useful planning window in Southern Ontario. The exact product and conditions still decide when painting can proceed: surfaces must be ready, temperatures suitable and the drying window long enough for the coating.

Discuss parking, garden furniture, pets and entrances before work begins. Ask how weather changes will be communicated, then review the finished surfaces and care guidance. Save the colour and product information for future maintenance.

title: Cabinet Painting vs Replacement: How to Decide
alt: Company painting photo collection: Cabinet Painting
excerpt: Compare cabinet painting and replacement by condition, layout and the complete work your kitchen needs.

sections.title: Decide whether appearance or layout needs to change
paragraphs: If the kitchen storage and layout work but the colour feels dated, cabinet painting may be worth considering. It refreshes suitable existing surfaces. Replacement can change cabinet construction, storage and configuration, so it solves a different set of problems.

List what you want to improve. Separate colour and surface wear from damaged boxes, poor storage or a layout that does not suit your household. That distinction helps the assessment and cost comparison.

sections.title: Check the cabinet material and condition
paragraphs: Review doors, drawers, fixed frames and exposed panels together. Wood, MDF, laminate and thermofoil need different assessments and preparation. Swollen areas, loose surface films or structural damage may point toward repairs or replacement before any painting is planned.
Ask about previous coatings, grease, worn edges and hardware handling. Confirm any carpentry separately. Assess boxes and panels separately from the doors.

sections.title: Plan a complete cabinet colour change
paragraphs: Compare colour samples beside the worktop, backsplash, flooring and the room’s lighting. Confirm sheen as well as shade. A contrasting island can work, but it should be reviewed with the perimeter cabinets rather than chosen in isolation.
Define visible coverage: doors, fronts, frames, island ends and exposed sides. Confirm backs, interiors and shelves separately. This helps avoid mismatched fronts and fixed surfaces.

sections.title: Compare painting and replacement costs fairly
paragraphs: Cabinet painting cost varies with component count, condition, preparation, access and the coating system. Compare a defined repainting scope with the replacement work you would actually need, including related installation and room changes. There is no guaranteed saving that fits every kitchen.
Ask about timing, drying and curing as well as price. Keep condition and goals central, with the work described in writing.

title: Surface Preparation Before Painting: What to Check
alt: Company painting photo collection: Project Planning
excerpt: Know which cleaning, coating preparation, repairs and priming details to review before a painting quote.

sections.title: Preparation supports paint adhesion
paragraphs: Paint needs a suitable surface beneath it. Dirt, grease, chalk and unstable coatings affect how the new finish adheres. Before discussing colour, review the existing material and what is needed to prepare it for the proposed coating.

Exterior siding and kitchen cabinets do not need an identical routine. Ask which cleaning, sanding, coating removal or priming steps apply to your surfaces and why. Follow product instructions for the condition.

sections.title: Separate painting preparation from repairs
paragraphs: Loose paint, damaged wood, lifting laminate and moisture stains need assessment. Some preparation belongs in the painting scope; failing materials or persistent water entry may require separate repair first. Covering the problem does not make the substrate sound.
Share known leaks, previous repairs and any information about older coatings. Unknown finishes should be assessed before they are disturbed. Ask how unexpected conditions and additions are agreed.

sections.title: Include protection and practical access
paragraphs: Preparation also means making the work area usable. Review protection for glazing, hardware, worktops, flooring or planting, depending on the project. The application method can influence the masking and clearance needed around the painted surfaces.
Confirm what you should move, which cabinets need clearing and which entrances must remain accessible. Include pets, vehicles and everyday use in the plan.

sections.title: Put preparation and products in the scope
paragraphs: A useful painting quote identifies surfaces, preparation, proposed primers and finish products. Confirm repairs, visible coverage and any excluded areas. Similar totals can include different amounts of work.

After painting, review the included surfaces and keep the colour, product and care information. Preparation is one part of the finish; suitable drying, curing and ongoing maintenance also deserve attention.

title: Exterior and Cabinet Paint Colours: How to Choose
alt: Company painting photo collection: Colour Ideas
excerpt: Choose exterior and cabinet colours around fixed materials, real lighting, suitable samples and sheen.

sections.title: Start with the finishes you are keeping
paragraphs: Roofing, brick, stone, worktops and flooring give a colour scheme its starting point. Look at their undertones before choosing paint. A shade that looks right on a screen may feel different beside those materials in your own home.
Collect a small set of examples that share the appearance you want. Compare the palette rather than recreating a photograph with different materials and light.

sections.title: Give the colour scheme a clear hierarchy
paragraphs: On an exterior, choose the role of siding, trim and the entrance. In a kitchen, consider the perimeter cabinets and island together. Decide which parts should blend in and which should provide a deliberate accent.
A consistent scheme does not need a different colour for every detail. Review the whole view, including surfaces that will not be painted.

sections.title: Check samples in the actual light
paragraphs: Review suitable samples beside the fixed finishes and in the lighting you normally use. For exterior paint colours, compare sunny and shaded elevations. For cabinets, check daylight and evening lighting before settling on the final shade.

Keep samples large enough to compare usefully, and avoid judging a colour only against white paper or a phone display. Confirm colour with the coating product; screens do not show the finished surface.

sections.title: Confirm material limits and sheen
paragraphs: Colour must suit the substrate as well as the design. Vinyl siding and some other components have manufacturer-specific colour guidance, so check compatibility before choosing a darker shade. The selected coating system should support the planned surface and use.
Confirm sheen with colour, then keep the final names, product details and included surfaces in your records. Keep these details for care, touch-ups and later painting.

title: Paint Finish Care: Curing, Cleaning and Maintenance
excerpt: Care for painted cabinets and exteriors with product-specific curing, cleaning and regular checks for wear.

sections.title: Dry paint and cured paint are different
paragraphs: A surface can feel dry before it is ready for normal handling, cleaning or loading. Ask for the instructions that apply to the actual coating and surface. Follow the manufacturer’s curing guidance rather than assuming one waiting period fits every paint.
Cabinet doors, shelves and exterior surfaces serve different purposes. Confirm when hardware can be handled, stored items replaced and cleaning resumed. Confirm these details before normal use.

sections.title: Keep the colour and product information
paragraphs: Save the colour name, sheen, coating product and agreed painting scope. Keep these records for advice, touch-ups or additional painting. Keep any written project-specific warranty with the same information.

If leftover paint is provided, ask how it should be labelled and stored. Follow the product instructions, and do not assume a touch-up will disappear perfectly on an older finish with a different application or wear pattern.

sections.title: Clean gently and watch for changes
paragraphs: Use the cleaning method recommended for the coating after the appropriate curing period. Check painted cabinet edges and areas near sinks for wear. Outdoors, inspect exposed details and places where water may collect, alongside the surrounding materials.

Discuss recurring staining, peeling or dampness before simply repainting. Surface marks and underlying problems need different responses. Painting cannot replace a repair that the substrate or building needs.

sections.title: Ask before repairing an uncertain area
paragraphs: If you are unsure whether to clean, touch up or repair a surface, ask for guidance about the product and condition. Abrasive treatment or an incompatible coating can turn a small issue into a larger finish problem.
Use your own project agreement for any warranty or follow-up terms. Website guides do not establish your project’s coverage or maintenance schedule.
